description: Ground-truth oracle for the usage-records fixtures consumed by the ADR-0038 usage-learner (the C engine). Each readable fixture lists the tool/command observations a learner MUST extract, the prompt cause each maps to (advisor-core PROMPT_CAUSES), and the expected generalized pattern + safety grade computed from the SHIPPED advisor-core (generalizeCommand + gradeCommand). Patterns/grades here are not hand-authored — they were produced by running each command through plugins/runtime/scripts/lib/{permission-sanitize,permission-advisor-core}.mjs, so a learner that diverges from these values has diverged from the shipped grader.
privacy: Every record is SYNTHETIC. Secret-shaped tokens are deliberately fake (EXAMPLEONLY / EXAMPLE markers) and exist ONLY to exercise redaction. No real secret, path, or transcript content appears in any fixture (ADR-0038 §5).

statuses.readable: File exists and is readable. A readable file that yields zero parseable records contributes no observations; if every source is empty the learner returns no_records_available. A directory/absent path is reported missing.
statuses.missing: Path does not exist. Loader returns status=missing, zero observations, and falls back to the conservative known-safe baseline (ADR-0038 §2). Represented as a filesystem state, NOT a committed file (see README).
statuses.permission-denied: Path exists but is not readable (e.g. mode 000 / EACCES). Loader returns status=permission-denied, zero observations, baseline fallback. Simulated at test time via chmod, NOT a committed file (see README).
statuses.malformed: File is readable but contains lines that are not valid JSON, or valid lines whose embedded tool arguments are not valid JSON. Loader skips the unparseable units and continues; partial extraction from the surviving lines is expected.

claude.WebFetch tool_use: claude.webfetch-domain (remedy allow-rule; rule key is the URL host)

codex.event_msg exec_approval_request (or appl: codex.approval-requested (remedy approval-policy) — the AUTHORITATIVE 'a prompt was produced' signal per the codex-cli 0.142.3 peer. A response_item carrying sandbox_permissions='require_escalated' only means the model REQUESTED escalation; key the cause off the event.
codex.event_msg exec_command_end whose aggrega: codex.sandbox-blocked (remedy sandbox-mode). Marker is Codex-specific: 'Command denied by sandbox:' / 'sandbox denied exec error' — NOT generic 'Permission denied' and NOT exit_code!=0 alone.
codex.mcp__<server>__<tool> function_call: codex MCP approval (host-specific; not in the two host-neutral Codex causes)

codex_command_normalization: A Codex shell command is an argv array — from local_shell_call.action.command (no JSON parse) OR from function_call(name='shell').arguments (a JSON string; parse it, then read .command). When command[0] is a shell (bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh) and command[1] is -lc/-c, the real command is command[2]; otherwise join the argv with spaces. Apply this BEFORE generalizeCommand/gradeCommand.
codex_schema_versioning: Confirmed against codex-cli 0.142.3 (peer). Line types include session_meta, turn_context, response_item, event_msg, inter_agent_communication, compacted (the local sample only exercises the first four). turn_context.payload carries the permission posture (sandbox_policy, approval_policy, permission_profile, workspace_roots) — the Codex analog of Claude's permission-mode entry. LEGACY DELTA: older rollouts use a function_call 'with_escalated_permissions' boolean instead of 0.142.3's sandbox_permissions enum (use_default|require_escalated|with_additional_permissions); a robust learner should tolerate both. function_call_output.output may be a string OR an array of {type:input_text|input_image|encrypted_content} items — normalize before marker-matching.

fixtures.notes: Mixed session covering all four Claude causes plus allow/ask/deny grades and a user-rejected command (the strongest prompt-cause signal).

Every command carries a SYNTHETIC secret-shaped token. generalizeCommand strips all arguments to '*' so no secret reaches the pattern; redactSecrets is the second line of defense for any kept token. The learner MUST NOT emit any rule/pattern/evidence containing the fragments in must_not_contain.

Line 1 permission-mode (valid), line 2 valid Bash, line 3 truncated JSON, line 4 empty, line 5 non-JSON garbage, line 6 valid Bash (recovery). The learner must skip the empty + the 2 unparseable lines and still extract from lines 2 and 6.

session_meta + turn_context (posture) + chat + two local_shell_call shapes + two function_call(name=shell) shapes + paired exec_command_end events + one exec_approval_request + one MCP call + task_complete. Each shell call is paired to its event by call_id. Covers BOTH shell shapes and BOTH event-based causes (codex-cli 0.142.3 authoritative).

observations.note: ran clean inside sandbox (exec_command_end exit_code=0, no denial marker) — informs baseline, not a prompt event

observations.sandbox_signal: paired exec_command_end.aggregated_output contains 'Command denied by sandbox:'

observations.approval_signal: a preceding event_msg exec_approval_request with the same call_id (authoritative); arguments also carry sandbox_permissions='require_escalated' + justification

observations.note: MCP call; not one of the two host-neutral Codex prompt causes

fixtures.notes: Line 1 session_meta, line 2 valid shell call, line 3 a VALID rollout line whose arguments string is non-JSON runaway text (real degenerate case), line 4 truncated/unparseable line, line 5 valid (recovery). Two distinct malformed sub-cases: an unparseable line AND a parseable line with unparseable embedded arguments.

observations.note: line parses but arguments is not JSON — skip this observation, do not crash
